title: PASTA: PARP activity screening and inhibitor testing assay
protocol: Bind His6-tagged target protein onto a 96-well Ni-NTA plate.
Incubate the bound protein at room temperature for 1 hour.
Prepare a 4× solution of 6-alkyne-NAD+ at 0.4 mM.
Set the final concentration of 6-alkyne-NAD+ to 100 μM for the enzymatic reaction.
Conduct the PARP enzymatic reaction in the presence of small-molecule inhibitors and 6-alkyne-NAD+.
Prepare 4× solutions of inhibitors from 800× DMSO stocks, including a DMSO control.
Add 1 μL of the DMSO stock to 199 μL PBR for each inhibitor.
Prepare a 2× compound/6-alkyne-NAD+ solution by combining equal volumes of each 4× compound dilution and 4× 6-alkyne-NAD+ solution.
Prepare a 2× solution of the PARP at 20 nM.
Incorporate activating cofactors into the 2× protein stock if required for specific PARPs (damaged DNA for PARP1 and PARP2, and 5′-nicked-dumbbell RNA for PARP3).
Measure enzymatic activity at a range of concentrations before testing compounds to ensure consistency across different batches of protein.
Remove target protein solution from the plate and wash plate 3× with 100 μL 1× PBST.
Wash plate once with 100 μL 1× PBS, followed by one wash with 100 μL PBR, leaving each wash for ≥2 min at RT.
Add 25 μL of 2× PARP solution to the 96-well plate.
Add 25 μL of 2× compound/6-alkyne-NAD+ to the 96-well plate.
Replace the 2× PARP solution with an equal volume of PBR if assessing auto-modification.
Incubate the plate at 30°C for 1 h after replacing PARP solution.
Mix biotin-N3 with the alkyne handle on 6-alkyne-ADP-ribose moieties now appended to the target protein on the plate.
Remove enzymatic reaction solution from the plate.
Wash the plate 3 times with 100 μL 1× PBST and once with 100 μL 1× PBS, leaving each wash for ≥2 min at RT.
Add 50 μL click reaction solution (100 μM TBTA, 1 mM CuSO4, 100 μM biotin-N3, 2 mM TCEP, 1× PBS) to the 96-well plate.
Prepare the complete click reaction solution within 10 min of use and ensure the TCEP is from an aqueous stock solution no more than 2 h old kept on ice.
Add TBTA first, followed by CuSO4, then biotin-N3, TCEP, 1× PBS, and DI water to the desired volume in sequence.
Incubate at 30°C for 30 minutes if the click reaction solution is not faintly blue.
Block with 1% milk to prevent non-specific Strep-HRP binding.
Remove the click reaction solution and wash the plate three times with 100 μL of 1× PBST, then once with 100 μL of 1× PBS, leaving each wash for at least 2 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of 1% milk in PBST to the 96-well plate.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove the milk block and wash the plate three times with 100 μL of 1× PBST, then once with 100 μL of 1× PBS, leaving each wash for at least 2 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of Strep-HRP (300 ng/μL BSA, 0.5 ng/μL Strep-HRP, 1× PBS) to the plate.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes.
Remove the Strep-HRP and wash the plate three times with 100 μL of 1× PBST, then once with 100 μL of 1× PBS, leaving each wash for at least 2 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare the QuantaRed solution immediately before adding it to the plate as per kit instructions.
Add 100 μL of QuantaRed solution to each well and incubate for 30 seconds to one minute.
Quench with the QuantaRed stop solution.
